name: Arcturus Defense Solutions Concussive Breach Charge CBC-3 'Knocker'
description: A shaped explosive charge designed specifically for breaching reinforced doors and walls without producing lethal fragmentation on the far side. The CBC-3 focuses its blast energy directionally into a narrow cone that defeats the structural integrity of the target barrier while minimizing overpressure on the breach side. The charge uses a water-tamped explosive that converts blast energy into a hydraulic ram effect, punching through doors and walls with less collateral risk than conventional explosives.
specifications:
charge type: Shaped water-tamped directional
breach capability: Reinforced steel doors, concrete block walls
fragmentation: Minimal — water tamping absorbs fragments
overpressure: Reduced by 70% vs conventional breach charges
weight: 0.8 kg per charge
placement: Magnetic adhesion to target surface
detonation: Manual, timed, or remote
story_hooks: CBC-3 charges were used to breach a vault but the water tamping failed — the resulting fragmentation killed a hostage on the other side of the door.
A stolen shipment of CBC-3 charges has given a criminal organization military-grade breaching capability that no commercial door or wall can resist.
related_entities: Carrion Defense Works Terrain Denial Foam Canister TDF-3

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact, disc-shaped charge with a pronounced conical depression on its breach face, resembling an inverted bell or mushroom cap. The form factor is deliberately flat and contoured for intimate contact with target surfaces. Despite its destructive purpose, it presents as an engineered, clinical object—more precision instrument than crude explosive.
physical_description.dimensions: 12 cm diameter × 8 cm height (charge body); conical breach face recesses 3 cm inward
physical_description.weight_description: Dense and substantial—0.8 kg feels concentrated and heavy for its compact size, suggesting high explosive density. Balanced when held flat, but the weight distribution toward the breach face creates a natural top-heavy impression.
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced polymer composite housing with internal water-tamping chamber; breach face is hardened ceramic-steel composite for directed energy focus
physical_description.finish: Matte tactical black polymer with subtle light-absorbing texture; the conical breach face has a darker, almost oil-slick metallic finish suggesting the ceramic-steel composite underneath
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary matte black with gunmetal-gray conical depression; Arcturus branding in silver-white; safety indicator strip in high-visibility orange running circumferentially
physical_description.grip_texture: Flat, slightly textured polymer top surface with integrated grip grooves; the back plate is smooth bare composite with subtle stippling for thumb purchase when placing charges
distinctive_features: Pronounced conical depression on breach face—the signature shaped charge geometry
Circumferential safety indicator strip (orange) that changes color if charge has been armed
Magnetic adhesion nodes recessed into the mounting plate (three contact points arranged triangularly)
Integrated detonator port on the side (threaded, sealed with a small red safety cap)
Arcturus Defense Solutions hexagonal logo stamped into the top surface
Small digital readout window (inert unless armed) showing charge status
Hairline thermal vent slots along the lower edge—barely visible but visible under angled light
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Arcturus Defense Solutions hexagonal logo centered on top surface in relief; serial number etched in small text below the logo; 'CBC-3 KNOCKER' designation stamped on the detonator side; manufacturing date code on the mounting plate
physical_description.condition_typical: Field units are usually pristine or lightly worn—these charges are stored carefully and deployed fresh. Well-maintained units show minimal scratching on the polymer body; the orange safety strip is always clean and legible. Used charges (post-detonation casings) would show blackened, cratered breach faces and melted safety strips.
